Q: as.character applied to factors in tibbles does not work when specifying specific rows A:

Tibble have the property that anytime you subset ([]) a tibble, you always get a tibble. That is a big difference between a data.frame which may simplify to a vector in some cases. The behavior can be inconsistent with data.frames but tibbles are consistent and predictable. Under the hood they are both lists.

So running class(t[1, "number"]) gives you a tibble while class(d[1, "number"]) gives you a factor

When you do

as.numeric(as.character(t[1, "number"]))

That's the same as

as.numeric(as.character(as.vector(t[1, "number"])))

In order to use the numeric and character functions, your input is coerced to a vector. So the object you are working with is

# as.vector(t[1, "number"])
$number
[1] 3
Levels: 2 3 5

And since vectors assign index to values based on the leve,s 3 is the second level so you get 2. But you have the issue that you are still working in the list rather than the factor vector itself.

If you are using tibbles, then the expectation is usually that you are using other tidyverse functions such as dplyr to manipulate them. So you could do

t |> mutate(number = as.numeric(as.character(number)))
#   name  number
#   <fct>  <dbl>
# 1 A          3
# 2 B          5
# 3 C          2

or the recommended way

t |> mutate(number = as.numeric(levels(number)))

Q: Is there an autosave function/plugin for Notepad++? A:

UPDATE 2022

For those who look for answear on similar question, I`ll try to give detailed description.

I`m personnaly use integrated backup/autosave for Notepad++ which, I think cover any needs for this functionality and better option can be only files versioning tools like git/hg etc.

So... Go to:
Settings / Preferences / Backup

This will open settings which containe two section:

  1. Session snapshot and periodic backup
  2. Backup on save

First option in first section is Remember current session for next launch:

After enable this, on restart NP++ will be open all session related instances, like opened files, project in projects panel etc, from previous session. But this may did not help if NP++ for some reason was unexpectedly closed(the process freezes, the power supply of the computer is interrupted, etc.) and as result you lost unsaved state of your files.

To partially protect against such an unpleasant accident, you can use the following option: Enable session snapshot and periodic backup:

After enable this, NP++ will after the interval specified in the option Backup in every N seconds, check all open and UNsaved in NP++ files, and save a copy of them with a timestamp in the file name extension(if in Windows explorer display extensions dissabled you can't see timestamp and see only filename wo extension), to the folder specified in the Backup path option.

d:\Temp\ff_stickers.js
d:\SYNCFOLDER\Settings\NP++\backup\ff_stickers.js@2022-04-19_141352

After you save original file, NP++ immediately delete this backup copy.
Also, enabling this option allows you to exit NP++ without saving opened and unsaved files. When you close the NP++, it does not prompt you to save opened and unsaved files, and the next time you open it, it displays them in the same way as before close - marked as unsaved.

Regarding the option Backup path - you cannot change this path, because it depends on where the NP++ configuration files are stored. By default, this is the folder backup in same folder where NP++ itself is located. In my case (on my screen), this path is located in the same place as the configuration files path, specified in the Cloud option:

Which was added to be able to synchronize NP++ settings.

The next options, already in the second section:
None
Simple backup
Verbose backup

With option Simple backup:

while you save original file in NP++, it will add *.bak file with previous saved state, next to the original:

d:\Temp\ff_stickers.js
d:\Temp\ff_stickers.js.bak

This *.bak remains the only one and is replaced on every save of original file.

With option Verbose backup:

while you save original file in NP++, it will add subfolder nppBackup next to the original file, and save there *.bak file with previous saved state.

d:\Temp\ff_stickers.js
d:\Temp\nppBackup\ff_stickers.js.2022-04-19_141952.bak

These files are not replaced when you save the original, and there are remain as many of them as you save the origanal file.

d:\Temp\ff_stickers.js
d:\Temp\nppBackup\ff_stickers.js.2022-04-19_141952.bak
d:\Temp\nppBackup\ff_stickers.js.2022-04-19_142717.bak
d:\Temp\nppBackup\ff_stickers.js.2022-04-19_142718.bak
d:\Temp\nppBackup\ff_stickers.js.2022-04-19_142719.bak
d:\Temp\nppBackup\ff_stickers.js.2022-04-19_142720.bak
d:\Temp\nppBackup\ff_stickers.js.2022-04-19_142721.bak
d:\Temp\nppBackup\ff_stickers.js.2022-04-19_142722.bak
d:\Temp\nppBackup\ff_stickers.js.2022-04-19_142723.bak
d:\Temp\nppBackup\ff_stickers.js.2022-04-19_142732.bak

And last option Directory, allows you to save *.bak files to a directory of your choice(here you can specify an arbitrary path).

d:\Temp\ff_stickers.js
d:\taravasya\BackUps\NPpp\ff_stickers.js.2022-04-19_143305.bak

Hope it help to use this great app and will save someone a lot of time and nerves))

Q: Font resource could not be retrieved A:

Ran into this problem while testing a new font selection app feature, and resolved it by following a idea of changing fonts suggested by the answer by Algorithm and Blues above.

I was using Google's variable monospace, sans-serif, and serif Roboto fonts with the intent of providing the same fonts all the way back to Android 5.0. The crashes started showing up using SDK 25.

At that point, on thinking about changing fonts to something similar, I tried using Google's static versions of the fonts in place of the variable versions. They worked fine. It seems that variable fonts are too new to the typography scene for the older Android versions to handle. So, use static fonts, and problem solved.

Except that I wanted to retain the variable versions to provide more font adjustablity features, like weight adjustability, at least in later Android versions. This problem was resolved by putting the static fonts in the app/main/res/font folder and the variable fonts in the app/main/res/font-26 folder, and then making sure the font names in each folder were identical (i.e. roboto_mono.ttf, etc.). With that arrangement, everything now works fine on the whole range of Android versions the app should support while enabling provision of the noted additional features.

Q: Python ctypes: how to use C stdio functions A:

If you have the fileno of a stream, you can use the C library to get a FILE* equivalent via fdopen(POSIX) or _fdopen(Windows):

Windows example:

import sys
import ctypes as ct

# typesafe FILE*
class FILE(ct.Structure): ...
PFILE = ct.POINTER(FILE)

clib = ct.CDLL('msvcrt')
clib.fprintf.argtypes = PFILE, ct.c_char_p,
clib.fprintf.restype = ct.c_int
clib._fdopen.argtypes = ct.c_int, ct.c_char_p
clib._fdopen.restype = PFILE

stderr = clib._fdopen(sys.stderr.fileno(), b'w')
clib.fprintf(stderr, b'%s, world!', b'hello')

Output:

hello, world!

Q: Dynamic query is producing duplicate columns A:

Duplicated columns is from "G.*" part of main query.
If you want leave only "Year" columns from subquery,
calculate years list as

SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(
         CONCAT(' (CASE WHEN G.`', Year, '` = ''O'' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ' )
         ORDER BY Year
         SEPARATOR ' + '
       )
         -- years list as G.`1890`,G.`1896`
    ,GROUP_CONCAT( distinct concat('G.`', Year, '`') order by year separator ',')
INTO @count_cols, @yearNames
FROM temp_years;

Result is

@count_cols= MAX(CASE WHEN MR.Year = 1890 THEN 'O' ELSE '-' END) AS `1890` , MAX(CASE WHEN MR.Year = 1896 THEN 'O' ELSE '-' END) AS `1896`

@yearNames = G.`1890`,G.`1896`

and in main query replace G.* with @yearNames

SET @sql := CONCAT(
'SELECT 
     G.Sport,
     G.Event,
     G.Gender,
     ', @count_cols, ' AS CountO,
         -- columns with years G.`1890`,G.`1896`
